name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,134

clue.text: Royal income’s half covered by news media

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word means keeping only its first three letters
something covered by another thing sits inside it, so the media word wraps around

blocks.note: the press is the news media collectively
the front half of the word income

explanation.surface: A royal's private finances being picked over by the tabloid papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Income is six letters, so its half is the first three; 'Royal' reads as an adjective but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a monarch's family, so she counts as a royal.

clue.text: Maybe piano phrase changed

indicators.note: letters that have been changed are put into a different order

blocks.note: p is the musical marking for piano, meaning soft
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician wondering whether a piano passage has been altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs expressing uncertainty about whether something is so.

clue.text: Deduce Hell is without number

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a piece is taken away from the word for hell

blocks.note: the inferno is hell, as in Dante
No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Someone concluding that hell has no numbers in it.
explanation.walkthrough: INFERNO loses its NO to leave INFER.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence, exactly as deducing does.

clue.text: Pantomime character recalled in breaks

indicators.note: when something breaks its pieces scatter and can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, both words

explanation.surface: An actor being called back on stage during intervals in a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reads as the verb of the surface, but it is just letters to rearrange together with 'in'. Pantomime is the British Christmas stage show for families.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella is one of the most popular stories staged as a British Christmas pantomime, and its heroine is a stock role.

clue.text: Jump, beginning to pogo in small circle

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
in places one piece inside the other pieces

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
the opening letter of pogo
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: Bouncing on a pogo stick inside a little circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a sudden leap upward or forward, so it serves as a synonym of a jump.

clue.text: Detect the best turns

indicators.note: something that turns faces the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the tops is a slang term for the very best

explanation.surface: Working out which of several twists is the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or catch sight of it, the same as detecting it.

clue.text: Drunken rave-up gatecrashed by northern upstart

indicators.note: a drunken thing staggers about out of order, so these letters are jumbled
a gatecrasher gets inside a party, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: the letters of rave-up rearranged
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A loud boozy party invaded by an uninvited northerner on the make.
explanation.walkthrough: A rave-up is a wild party; N goes into the rearranged PARVEU between E and U.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a person who has risen suddenly in wealth or status and is seen as not belonging, an upstart.

clue.text: Doctor rates provider of shocking treatment

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician grading a supplier of electroconvulsive therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a medical person in the scene, but it is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a weapon that fires darts delivering an electric jolt, a witty take on giving someone a shock.

clue.text: Plant’s extremely rare elaborate decoration

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of rare
finery is showy, elaborate clothing or ornament

explanation.surface: A garden plant that is notable for its unusual, ornate appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a flower in the surface but means a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is an industrial installation for purifying oil or sugar, and plant is a word for such a works.

clue.text: King returned gentleman’s dagger

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the title is read backwards

blocks.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
sir is the title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A monarch giving back a nobleman's knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay or Indonesian blade with a wavy edge, a kind of short sword or knife.

clue.text: Job control under a foreign power

blocks.note: first meaning: a person's line of work
second meaning: a territory held and run by another country's forces

explanation.surface: A post that involves governing on behalf of another nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both one's trade or employment and military seizure and holding of territory by an outside state.

clue.text: Meagre enemies partially concur

indicators.note: partially means only part of the words is used, so the answer is concealed inside them

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Sparse foes coming round to the same view in part.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to be of the same opinion, which is what concurring means.

clue.text: After bringing forward note, ambiguous about energy?

indicators.note: bringing something forward lifts it from its place and sets it at the front

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for note
something ambiguous is unclear

explanation.surface: Someone vague on the subject of power after a musical note is moved ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The N in UNCLEAR is moved from second place to the front, giving N-UCLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear power is a major energy source, so the adjective describes things concerning that kind of power, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Adder’s venom finally treated with serum

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
treated means processed or worked on, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: the closing letter of venom
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snake bite being treated with antivenom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adder' looks like the snake, which the venom and serum support, but it means one who adds up, pronounced SUM-er.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sums figures is a summer, a crossword-only sense of a word that normally names the season.

clue.text: Second bishop in valley is not fixed

indicators.note: in places the cleric piece inside the landscape piece

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a vale is a valley
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A runner-up cleric living in a valley has no settled home.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is a British informal word for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something movable can be shifted from place to place, so it is not fixed in position.

clue.text: Faculty regularly joining core trio of alumnae fall for some

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is kept
the core is the centre, so the three middle letters are taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of faculty
the three central letters of alumnae

explanation.surface: University staff and female graduates coming together, with some of them falling for each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall for' reads as falling in love, but fall is the North American name for the season.
explanation.definitionFit: In North American English the season after summer is called fall, so for some speakers it is their word for autumn.

clue.text: Walk in the park on waste ground

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stroll in a park built on derelict land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like land in the surface, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a task that is very easy, needing no effort at all.

clue.text: Victory period does not include last season

indicators.note: not including the last means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a win is a victory
a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: A spell of triumph that leaves out the previous season.
explanation.walkthrough: TERM loses its last letter to give TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter is the coldest of the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: He scored 50 on oral exam I’d brought back

indicators.note: brought back means returned the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a viva is an oral examination
L is the Roman numeral for 50
I'd without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A student boasting of getting 50 marks on a spoken test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' suggests marks, but it means wrote a musical score; the 50 sits after VIVA though the clue puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivaldi was the Italian Baroque composer of The Four Seasons, so he wrote out musical scores.

clue.text: Clergyman cut grass border

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a verger is a church official who looks after the building

explanation.surface: A churchman mowing the lawn edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like mowing grass but tells you to clip VERGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is the strip of grass along the edge of a road or path.

clue.text: Store’s first-class service

blocks.note: A as in A1 or grade A stands for top quality
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A shop boasting of its excellent customer service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' reads as customer care but means a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To store things is to gather and accumulate a stock of them, which is what amassing means.

clue.text: Entertain a writer’s inspiration?

blocks.note: taken as written
a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

explanation.surface: Is a writer's source of ideas simply there to keep them diverted?
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to hold their attention pleasantly, which is entertaining them.

clue.text: Medal attached to queen’s gown

indicators.note: attached to means fixed on after something, so the medal follows the royal letter

blocks.note: R is short for Regina, Latin for queen
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An honour pinned to the monarch's dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the medal is attached to the queen, so OBE goes after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose outer garment, the same as a gown.

clue.text: Antagonistic manner and posture

blocks.note: first meaning: a hostile, uncooperative way of behaving
second meaning: a position of the body, as in ballet

explanation.surface: Someone combative in both their behaviour and their stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means truculent behaviour, and it also names a bodily pose or stance.

clue.text: Eg Jacob’s mate runs vessel

blocks.note: a Jacob is a breed of spotted sheep, so its mate is a female sheep
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Biblical Jacob's wife hurrying off with a container.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob suggests the patriarch of Genesis, whose wife Rachel's name means ewe, but here it is the sheep breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug for water, a vessel for holding liquid.

clue.text: Swirling patterns in part of church

indicators.note: swirling means twisting about, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Whirling designs decorating a church interior.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is the cross arm of a cruciform church, running across the nave.
